Subject: Recap and next steps — deployment mode for PoC

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of requirements (from our notes):
- Primary use case: customer support automation for high-volume tickets (~2k/day) with 95th pct latency target of <200ms for synchronous requests.
- Data sensitivity: PII in support transcripts; legal wants SOC2 + encrypted-at-rest and separation between dev and prod data.
- Expected throughput: spike to ~300 concurrent requests during peak.
- Success criteria for PoC: 1) avg latency <200ms on representative workload, 2) no data persisted to Redwood logs (customer-managed keys), 3) model quality parity with current baseline on 5 eval prompts (F1/accuracy targets included in attached template).
- Stakeholders: Daniel Reed (Engineering), Aisha Ahmed (Head of ML), Procurement (TBD), Security (TBD).

Deployment mode considerations we discussed:
- Hosted API: fastest to get started, easiest from an operational standpoint.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPUs for predictable throughput and isolation; good middle ground if you want predictable SLOs.
- Private VPC / on-prem: required if Security insists on no cross-tenant control plane or for certain regulatory constraints.

Proposed PoC plan (high level):
1) Week 0: Agree on success criteria and sample dataset (I attached the PoC template).
2) Week 1–2: Sandbox run (Hosted API) to validate model choice and prompts with synthetic dataset.
3) Week 3: If throughput/latency or security require, spin up Dedicated capacity and repeat subset of tests.
4) Week 4: Optional Private VPC trial (if procurement/security require) — this typically takes longer for network setup.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm the primary decision driver (latency/cost/security/regulatory)?
- Please share the primary security contact and procurement timeline.
- I've attached a redwood-poc-template.pdf with success criteria and a short data checklist — fill what you can and send back.

If it helps, I can schedule a 30-min technical kickoff next week with Ben (solutions engineer) and Marissa (CS) to lock down test vectors and timeline.

Thanks,

Hi Daniel / Aisha —

Thanks — useful context. Quick update on what I recommend and why: 

Recommendation: Start with Hosted API for the initial quality and prompt engineering verification (Week 1–2). Simultaneously prepare a Dedicated capacity config as a fallback for Week 3 if you see throughput/latency or if Security requires stronger isolation. We typically run this gate as a binary decision after the Hosted sandbox: if no-logs + KMS integration and latency are within targets, we continue on Hosted; otherwise, move to Dedicated.

Rationale: Hosted lets us iterate on prompts and model variants much faster. Dedicated short-circuits operational variability and gives you reserved GPU capacity and stronger data isolation controls; Private VPC is the most secure but has the biggest lead time (network + VPN + MSA).

Proposed concrete PoC timeline (adjustable):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria (please confirm the 3 bullets I listed earlier) and share the eval set.
- Week 1: Hosted sandbox — Redwood provides a no-logs configuration (we’ll disable persistence and enable customer KMS for any transient artifacts). Our security docs will include SOC2 attestation and the controls we can provide.
- Week 2: Run representative traffic (we’ll provide a replay harness) and collect latency/throughput.
- Week 3: If needed, spin up Dedicated reserved pool to validate stable 95th percentile latency and repeat critical tests.
- Week 4: Optional Private VPC trial if InfoSec requires on-prem or segregated control plane.

Action items: 
- Aisha: can you share the eval prompts and a representative sample of tickets by EOD Monday?
- Daniel: please provide InfoSec primary contact and any minimum MSA/contract requirements — procurement wants the MSA draft to start parallel conversations.
- Marissa (cc’d): can you own the internal SRE/solutions engineering coordination for a Dedicated spin-up (if we go that route)?

I attached the PoC template again for quick completion. I’ll also prepare a short runbook for the Hosted no-logs config and a checklist for Dedicated transition.
